solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Direction in trial causing great sadness

indicators.note: in tells us the word for direction sits inside the word for a trial

parts.note: a hearing is a trial in a court of law
a trend is a direction or general tendency

explanation.surface: A judge's instruction during a court case causes great distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direction' reads like a judge's instruction to a jury, but it is a trend, a tendency.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that wrings the heart is deeply distressing, causing great sadness: a straightforward synonym.

parts.note: a habit is a routine practice

explanation.surface: Someone's usual routine of staying at home.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's natural home or environment is its habitat, a near synonym.

indicators.note: missing says the article must be left out of the yearbook word

parts.note: an annual is a book published each year
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone cancels the validity of a yearbook that lacks an article.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the two As in ANNUAL goes, leaving ANNUL.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a contract or marriage is to declare it void, to invalidate it.

parts.note: temper is anger, as in losing one's temper
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone keeps their fury in check over a written note.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means the anger word sits on top of A and TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperate means moderate and self-restrained, so controlled in behaviour or appetite.

indicators.note: over in a down clue signals the word is turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: made can mean reached, as in made it to the station

explanation.surface: Someone stretched across the table for the cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a Dutch cheese with a red wax rind, an example of the class.

indicators.note: involving means the rearranged letters wrap around the abbreviation
shocking suggests the letters of the diaries word are jolted into a new order

explanation.surface: Scandalous diaries implicate a Liberal prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking' rearranges DIARIES to DISRAEI, and 'involving' puts L inside, before the final I. Disraeli was in fact a Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was twice the British Prime Minister in the nineteenth century, an example of a PM.

clue.text: Girl, I complain, has been set up

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means raised, so the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to moan is to complain

explanation.surface: A girl grumbles that she has been framed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has been set up' turns the whole of I MOAN upwards, giving NAOMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a girl's given name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: From now on batting must get tense

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is said to be in
the future is a grammatical tense

explanation.surface: From now on, the batsman will have to feel nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like nervousness, but it is the grammatical tense.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means from this point onwards, henceforth, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Handsome youth is standing behind a fellow

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is stands below, after, the other pieces

parts.note: a don is a college fellow at a university such as Oxford

explanation.surface: A handsome young man stands behind a university fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite, so the name is used for any handsome young man.

clue.text: Definitely not taking foreign money in bars

indicators.note: in means the reworked money letters sit inside the word for bars

parts.note: to bar something is to ban it

indicators.note: foreign suggests the letters are made strange, rearranged

explanation.surface: Bars certainly will not accept foreign currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' looks like pubs to drink in, but here it is a verb, meaning bans or forbids.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom is an emphatic negative, meaning certainly not, not at all.

indicators.note: imprisoning shows the scrambled letters close around the abbreviation
wrong indicates the letters of done are put the wrong way, rearranged

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogies

explanation.surface: A man had wronged his wife by locking her up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges DONE to ONED, and 'imprisoning' puts W inside, after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: To have possessed something is to have had it, a past-tense synonym.

definitions.meaning: a cashier who serves customers at a bank counter
a person who counts votes in an election or parliamentary division

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a bank clerk at the counter and a person who tallies votes.

clue.text: Saying little, soldiers about revolution on island

indicators.note: on in an across clue places the revolution word after the island letter

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers
C is short for circa, Latin for about
a turn is one revolution of a wheel

explanation.surface: Quiet soldiers talk about an uprising on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests an uprising but is a single turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A taciturn person is reserved and uncommunicative, so habitually saying little.

indicators.note: holding means the giant's word contains the numeral

parts.note: a titan is a giant, like the biblical Goliath
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An artist asks whether he painted Goliath clutching a single item.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was a great Venetian Renaissance painter, so he is a man who painted.

clue.text: Those people getting shrewd in rulership

indicators.note: getting means the pronoun receives the other word inside it

parts.note: they is the pronoun for those people
arch can mean cunning or shrewd

explanation.surface: Those people become cunning when given power to rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Thearchy is rule by a god or gods, a rare word for divine government or rulership.

clue.text: The whole lot facing individuals in college

indicators.note: facing places the first word before, in front of, the second

parts.note: all means the whole lot
souls are individual people, as in not a soul

explanation.surface: Everyone faces each person individually at a college.
explanation.walkthrough: All Souls is an Oxford college with no undergraduates.
explanation.definitionFit: All Souls College, Oxford, is a famous graduate-only college, an example of the class.

indicators.note: resorts read as re-sorts says the letters are sorted again

explanation.surface: Spanish wine bars at holiday resorts were vandalised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resorts' looks like holiday spots but is read as re-sorts. A bodega is a Spanish wine bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To sabotage something is to wreck it deliberately, so the past tense matches wrecked.

parts.note: even so means still, nevertheless

explanation.surface: A church service is still no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' is the phrase EVEN SO, nevertheless, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service, an example of a church service.

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the pupil's word

parts.note: to book a seat is to reserve it

explanation.surface: Jam is mentioned in a schoolchild's first reading book.
explanation.definitionFit: Preserve is fruit cooked with sugar and stored, a synonym for jam.

clue.text: Tree liked by one's associates — not yew, by the sound of it

indicators.note: not means the letter is removed from the longer word

parts.note: popular means liked by one's peers

indicators.note: the tree name yew is said aloud, giving the letter that sounds the same

parts.note: the tree name yew is pronounced like the letter U

explanation.surface: A tree is well liked by its companions, though it is not a yew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yew' looks like a second tree, but here it stands for the letter U, whose name sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The poplar is a tall fast-growing tree of the willow family, an example of a tree.

definitions.meaning: an aim or purpose, stressed on the first syllable as a noun
to protest against something, stressed on the second syllable as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a goal or purpose; as a verb it means to raise an objection.

clue.text: Disease in tuna at sea revealed during short examination

indicators.note: revealed during means the scrambled fish appears inside the shortened word
short says the exam word loses its last letter

parts.note: a test is an examination

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Illness in tuna at sea emerged during a brief medical check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last letter of the exam word, and 'at sea' scrambles the fish, which then sits between the second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus, or lockjaw, is a bacterial infection causing muscle spasms, an example of a disease.

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters are changed in order

explanation.surface: A paler sun has damaged a kitchen herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Purslane is a fleshy plant used in salads and cooking, an example of a pot-herb.

indicators.note: used in says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Technical jargon is used when emailing other people.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is informal for specialist language or jargon, a synonym.

clue.text: Finest drop of milk stout drunk

indicators.note: drunk means the letters are reeling, rearranged
a drop of is a small amount, here just the first letter of the dairy word

explanation.surface: The best thing is a little milk in a stout once drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges M with STOUT to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Utmost means greatest or extreme, so the best or highest degree, here the finest.

parts.note: out can mean mistaken, as in your guess is out
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is wrong about an odd character.
explanation.definitionFit: Outre, from French, means unconventional or bizarre, so eccentric.

parts.note: gal is an informal word for girl

explanation.surface: A girl enjoys a special day out.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive public occasion, so a field day of celebration.

clue.text: A female, nervous at first, pale-faced

parts.note: she is the female pronoun

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of the word nervous

explanation.surface: A woman is nervous at the start and looks pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means grey like ash, so pale-faced from shock or fear.

clue.text: Primate called, absorbed by published article

indicators.note: absorbed by means the telephoned word is taken inside the published word

parts.note: out means published, as in the book is out
rang means called on the telephone
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone phoned and was engrossed in a magazine article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' could suggest a bishop, but here it is the ape.
explanation.definitionFit: The orangutan is a great ape of Borneo and Sumatra, an example of a primate.

indicators.note: high suggests the letters are intoxicated, and so rearranged

explanation.surface: The film High Society lies out of reach.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic High Society is another film title; 'High' is the anagram signal for BEYOND GRASP, and S comes from Society. Porgy and Bess, Gershwin's opera, was filmed in 1959.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gershwin opera was made into a Hollywood musical film in 1959, an example of a film.
